main_issue: Whether and how Agent D can keep cooking strong-smelling fried salted fish in the shared kitchen, given the smell affects the others' rooms, laundry and work

A-B.evidence: A asks for no strong-smelling cooking (1); B agrees the smell is bad (2) and later accepts D's weekend plan with notice (14), so both end on the same arrangement without addressing each other.

A-C.evidence: C backs the complaint about smell (3), later accepts the weekend plan with the door closed (16), as A does (11).

A-D.evidence: D says the cooking is normal (4) and A holds firm (5); then D offers once a week on weekends with notice and the yard door closed (10), and A says a weekend works (11).

B-C.evidence: B (8) and C (9) both say the smell is still a problem after 7 p.m.; both later accept D's weekend plan (14, 16).

B-D.evidence: B says the smell is still a problem after 7 (8); D proposes the weekly weekend plan with notice (10), and B accepts if told beforehand so they can close their door (14).

C-D.evidence: C says the smell still gets into the laundry in the evenings (9); D asks if the plan is okay (15), and C accepts if it is on a weekend with the door closed (16).
